Special Council Meeting - Workplan SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AND PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
JOINT SPECIAL MEETING
MINUTES
TUESDAY, JUNE 19, 2007
04:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S. HIGHWAY 101,
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
Present:
Heebner, Kellejian, Roberts, Nichols, and Campbell.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
Leticia Rodriguez, Deputy City Clerk
Steve Didier, Management Analyst
Park Morse, Interim Deputy City Manager
Mary Blais, Interim Community Dev. Dir.
Dennis Coleman, Finance Dir.
Chandra Collure, City Engineer
FLAG SALUTE:
Roger Boyd led the flag salute.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols Motion carried unanimously.
1.
City Council Strategic Planning
A.
Discussion and prioritization of the City of Solana Beach, the Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency, and the Solana Beach Public Financing Authority for Fiscal Year 2007/08 Workplan.
Draft Workplan
Roger Boyd stated that Fletcher Cove looks great, that there should be a phase II of this project, that the Lifeguard Station needs to be renovated to be more compatible with the new park, that temporary fixes at La Colonia Park should be considered with long term renovations, that fixing the basketball court may not be compatible with future designs of the park, that safety should be thought about with the I-5 interchange project, that the temporary north bound exit is a concern, and that the citizens need to be protected. He stated that renovation of the eastern side of the City should be considered one project because it impacts the traffic flow on that side of the City, and he encouraged the Council to continue neighborhood traffic studies.
Chandra Collure, City Engineer, stated that Caltrans would install an electric sign between Lomas Santa Fe and Villa De La Valle informing drivers that they need to slow down due to construction.
Patricia Hogan stated that she had several issues with neighbors on vegetation heights, that due to increased population ordinances are required for enacting laws in the City, and that there needs to be vegetation control. She stated that she won a view assessment case in 1990, that the applicant also planted vegetation and the trees would grow high enough to block her water and sunset view, that she addressed this issue with the neighbor and the neighbor refused to offer any compromise, that a neighbor to her north planted bamboo, and that she thinks there should be a vegetation ordinance so people do not take issues into their own hands.
Leslie Smith (3 minutes donated by Jim Smith) stated that she had concerns over view and vegetation issues in the City. She stated that tackling the whole issue would be very complex, that Council start by addressing "vegetation as a fence" as a first issue to tackle, that there is already an ordinance regarding fences, that her neighbor planted bamboo, that it had grown like a fence around the back yard, that this is a common issue in the City, and that she would assist Council in this effort.
Wayne Bretchel (3 minutes donated by Nick Nicholas) stated that he was speaking on behalf of Nick Nicholas, that there is a conflict between the General Plan and Zoning and Subdivision Ordinance, that he had spoken to Council on a parcel split that Mr. Nicholas had requested, that Mr. Nicholas would like to bring back another application, and if Mr. Nicholas were to build the design in conformance with the General Plan he would be out of conformance with the subdivision ordinance, and that this is a conlflict that did not apply to many parcels, and requested that Council and Staff look at the conflict between the General Plan, Zoning Ordinance, and Subdivision Ordinance.
Mayor Heebner read the objectives of the three strategic priorities which include, Community Character, Fiscal Sustainability, and Organizational Effectiveness.
Council discussed the strategic priorities, that conflicts exist within the three priorities, that there is no guidance on how issues impact each other within the various areas of the priorities, and that all three pieces have to work with each other.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that all the priorities are interdependent of each other and that Staff could add statements to the workplan to note this.
Council discusssion ensued on additions to the mission statement, that there are regional impacts on decisions that Council makes such as the I-5 Interchange project, that these impacts should be noted in the workplan, that certain projects are done for the region that impact the City, and that those influences need to be balanced with the priorities.
Council discussed conflicts between the Zoning Ordinance and the General Plan, that the citizens of the City should be involved as they were in the forming of the initial document, and that community input should be taken on this document.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that reviewing and updating the General Plan is a long process due to all the community input and workshops involved, that everything falls under the General Plan, that community involvement is important, and that a broad base of stake holders should be included.
Council discussion ensued on looking at the General Plan, that areas of conflict should be addressed first, that the process could take many years without specific focus, that a survey could be submitted to the community, that the City needs to utilize experts to work on the General Plan, that other cities require many different professionals to review General Plans, and that the City should make this document a priority.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that the City is aware of several issues that need to be addressed within the General Plan, that revising the General Plan did not only include conflicts within the plan but also addressing issues changing within the City including, parking issues, outdoor dining, signs, and other changes in the City.
Council discussion ensued that the City’s goal was to adopt a Local Coastal Plan by June 2007, that a sand retention program was needed in addition to a replenishment program, and that Council would like a presentation of the placement of tubes underground for sand replenishment, and that the program requires existing sand on the beach in order to retain it.
Council discussion ensued on the creation of a view and vegetation ordinance, that the issue was more complex than originally thought, that there was a lot of community support for this topic, and that there should be sprecific definitions, and that Council would be looking for community input on this topic in August 2007.
Council discussion continued on the view and vegetation ordinance, that there should be an educational pamplet to define problems and solutions, and a process similar to that of the View Assessment Committee should be considered.
Council discussion ensued on an RFP for a sign consultant to do an inventory of public and private signs and provide the City with guidelines on how to develop a signage program.
Council reviewed the list of Capital Improvement Projects, which included the ADA Plan, Fletcher Cove Improvement Project, and that Council would like a staus report on this project. Additional projects included the La Colonia Park Improvements, I-5 Interchange project, and the I-5 widening project, and Council expressed concerns regarding sound walls for the I-5 project.
Council discussion ensued on additional items for the section "Other Community Character Priorities" such as the East Side Community Center Study, Sidewalks on Lomas Santa Fe to Sunny Valley, St. Leo’s Crosswalk, and the Responsible Beverage Sales and Service (RBSS) ordinance, the issue of mini dorms in Solana Beach, the addition of a Senior Recognition Program, and adding a pedestrian gate at San Dieguito Park. Other additions included the North Cedros Standards, and moving the post office to a more centralized area in the City.
Council discussion ensued on the possible addition of solar panels to City facilites and whether to consider expediting permits to applicants whose projects were environmentally sensitive.
Council discussed banning plastic bag and rock advertising in the City, that the City should review affordable housing options, that regulations should be reviewed to prevent existing commercial parking overflow into residential areas, and that Council needed a method to prioritize items on the workplan.
Council and City Manager discussion ensued on how to prioritize items for Staff on the Council workplan, that Council should chose a top five list within each category, and that there would be an additional meeting for the workplan.
Council discussion ensued on the Views and Vegetation Committee, whether there should be a wide range of professionals on the committee such as an arborist and other professionals with expertise related to the issue and that a finance and feasibility study be conducted for construction of a parking structure on the distillery lot parking area.
Council and City Manager discussion ensued on performance measurements being implemented by the City which would allow the City to gauge services that are being provided and would provide feedback for the City and residents.
Mayor Heebner adjourn the meeting at 5:27 p.m.
ADJOURN:
____________________________________
Leticia Rodriguez, Deputy City Clerk
